_meta.description: Drugs that failed a human ALS trial. Hand-curated, because there is no downloadable dataset of ALS trial failures. This is the negative control set for the KG ranking and the input to the never_arrived / arrived_failed partition.
_meta.verification: Every year and phase was checked against a source fetched at curation time, not asserted from memory. 29 of 32 entries have both year and phase confirmed by the cited source and carry verified: true. The 3 entries with verified: false are pre-registry trials whose publications state no phase; the phase there comes from a secondary review and the verify_note names it.
_meta.year_semantics: year is the year of the source cited - the year the negative result was published or announced. Where a sponsor announced failure earlier than the journal publication, the note or verify_note says so. Four HEALEY regimens stopped dosing in 2022 but published in 2025; arimoclomol failed publicly in 2021 and published in 2024.
_meta.phase_semantics: The phase of the trial that failed, not the highest phase the drug ever reached.
_meta.bucket: Deliberately null. Component B (bbb_model.py) owns the partition and fills bbb_prob and bucket. A guess here would corrupt the headline result.
_meta.structures: SMILES came from PubChem by name and were checked against PubChem's Title and MolecularFormula so the structure matches the right drug, including single enantiomers where the drug is one. 26 of 32 entries have a SMILES. The other 6 are oligonucleotides, proteins, a random copolymer and a gold nanocrystal suspension, which have no practical SMILES - component B should refuse to score them rather than guess, which is the applicability-domain behaviour we want to demonstrate.
deliberate_exclusions: fingolimod - the 2017 phase 2a (NCT01786174, n=30, 4 weeks) MET its primary safety and tolerability endpoint and was never powered for efficacy. Including it as a failure would be wrong and a judge could catch it.

deferiprone - FAIR-ALS II (NCT03293069) is real, phase 2/3 and completed, but no result has ever been published or announced (ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults = false). We cannot call a trial failed when nobody has reported it.
riluzole and edaravone - these work, and they are the positive controls, not graveyard entries.
tofersen - accelerated approval stands; VALOR missed its primary endpoint but the drug is approved, so it is not a clean failure.
_meta.sources: Primary literature via PubMed/PMC, ClinicalTrials.gov registry records, and sponsor or consortium announcements where no peer-reviewed primary results paper exists (PHOENIX, TUDCA-ALS, BIIB078, glatiramer acetate, talampanel).

graveyard.name: ceftriaxone
graveyard.note: raised glial glutamate transporter EAAT2 in models; no stage 3 benefit
graveyard.note_extra: A seamless combined phase 1/2/3; stage 3 is the failed efficacy stage. The anchor case for the signed barrier rule - a central target in a drug with poor CNS penetration.

graveyard.name: minocycline
graveyard.note: anti-apoptotic, anti-inflammatory tetracycline; function declined faster than placebo
graveyard.note_extra: Actively harmful, not merely inert. Worth saying out loud: a screening tool that ranks drugs by plausibility would have ranked this well.

graveyard.name: lithium carbonate
graveyard.note: neuroprotective in cell and animal models; no survival benefit at 18 months
graveyard.note_extra: An inorganic salt. Fingerprint-based descriptors are close to meaningless here, so expect component B to report it out of domain - which is the correct behaviour.

graveyard.name: creatine
graveyard.note: mitochondrial ATP buffering and pore stabilization; no strength or function benefit
graveyard.verify_note: Year 2008 confirmed from the publication, which states no phase. PHASE3 and enrollment 107 come from registry record NCT00069186, matched to the paper by investigator (Rosenfeld, Carolinas) and enrollment. Two other creatine trials also failed - Groeneveld 2003 (n=175) and Shefner 2004 (n=104) - but were not phase 3.

graveyard.name: coenzyme q10
graveyard.note: mitochondrial antioxidant cofactor; futile at 2700 mg, phase 3 unwarranted
graveyard.note_extra: 863 Da with ten isoprene units. Expect out of domain, and expect the honest answer to be that nothing this lipophilic and this large was ever going to partition predictably.

graveyard.name: topiramate
graveyard.note: AMPA antagonist reducing glutamate excitotoxicity; arm strength declined faster
graveyard.verify_note: Year 2003, n=296 and the negative result are confirmed, but the publication states no phase and the trial (enrolled 1999-2000) predates ClinicalTrials.gov. Phase 2 comes from the Berry/Cudkowicz/Shefner review (PMID 24588460), which calls it 'this large phase II trial'.

graveyard.name: celecoxib
graveyard.note: COX-2 inhibition of neuroinflammation; no strength, function, or survival benefit
graveyard.verify_note: Year 2006, n=300 and the negative result are confirmed, but the Annals of Neurology paper states no phase and the trial predates registry registration. '2/3' comes from the Petrov 2017 review trial table in Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience.

graveyard.name: memantine
graveyard.note: NMDA receptor antagonism against excitotoxicity; no ALSFRS-R or survival benefit
graveyard.note_extra: MND-SMART phase 3 (n=554) is the pivotal failure. An earlier single-centre phase 2/3 (n=63, PMID 20565333) also failed.

graveyard.name: dexpramipexole
graveyard.note: candidate mitochondrial neuroprotectant; no benefit on combined function-survival score
graveyard.note_extra: The enantiomer of pramipexole, chosen to drop the dopaminergic activity. A phase 2 signal that did not survive phase 3 - the canonical ALS story.

graveyard.name: tirasemtiv
graveyard.note: fast skeletal troponin activator boosting muscle force; slow vital capacity unchanged
graveyard.note_extra: The precedent for the signed barrier rule. A muscle target in a brain-penetrant molecule; Cytokinetics rebuilt the mechanism as reldesemtiv to stay peripheral.

graveyard.name: reldesemtiv
graveyard.note: next-generation fast troponin activator; stopped for futility on ALSFRS-R
graveyard.note_extra: Tirasemtiv's successor, designed to stay out of the CNS, and it still failed. The honest reading: fixing the delivery problem does not fix a wrong mechanism. This pair is the single best illustration of the partition.

graveyard.name: gabapentin
graveyard.note: reduced glutamate synthesis in models; no slowing of strength decline
graveyard.note_extra: WALS study group; no trial acronym or NCT. Also fails our patient filter twice over - FDA respiratory-depression warning, and a CNS target it is predicted not to reach.

graveyard.name: pentoxifylline
graveyard.note: PDE inhibitor lowering TNF-alpha; survival worse than placebo
graveyard.verify_note: The abstract confirms 2006 and worse-than-placebo survival but does not self-label the phase; sponsor and press coverage call it the phase 3 trial (400 patients, 12 European centres).

graveyard.name: xaliproden
graveyard.note: oral neurotrophic 5-HT1A agonist; no significant survival benefit
graveyard.verify_note: 2004 is the publication year of the negative report; the two trials ('Study 1' and 'Study 2') completed around 2000.

graveyard.name: talampanel
graveyard.note: non-competitive AMPA receptor antagonist; missed ALSFRS-R primary endpoint
graveyard.verify_note: Registry gives PHASE2, 559 patients, completion 2010-05; the failed primary endpoint was announced in Teva's ALSTAR press release of 17 May 2010. No peer-reviewed publication of the 559-patient trial exists. Do not cite PMID 19961264 for this - that is the earlier 59-patient phase 2, which was mildly encouraging.

graveyard.name: mecasermin
graveyard.note: recombinant IGF-1 neurotrophic support; no benefit over two years
graveyard.verify_note: 70-residue recombinant protein; PubChem returns no CID. 2008 is the publication year; follow-up ended August 2007.

graveyard.name: valproic acid
graveyard.note: HDAC inhibitor raising SMN protein; no survival or function effect

graveyard.name: thalidomide
graveyard.note: TNF-alpha lowering immunomodulator; no benefit, significant toxicity
graveyard.verify_note: Single-arm open-label phase 2 (Stommel et al., 23 enrolled, 18 evaluable) against historical controls; no acronym or NCT.

graveyard.name: ozanezumab
graveyard.note: anti-Nogo-A antibody to restore neuromuscular junctions; no efficacy
graveyard.verify_note: Humanised monoclonal antibody; no PubChem CID. A ~150 kDa antibody against a peripheral neuromuscular-junction target - the opposite delivery problem from a CNS small molecule.

graveyard.name: rasagiline
graveyard.note: MAO-B inhibitor neuroprotection; no survival difference versus placebo
graveyard.note_extra: Clears all eight patient-filter rules for Alex. The trial_history stage, not the patient filter, is what should catch it - which is exactly why the graveyard is a pipeline stage and not a footnote.

graveyard.name: levosimendan
graveyard.note: calcium sensitiser boosting diaphragm force; no respiratory function benefit
graveyard.verify_note: 2021 is the Lancet Neurology publication year; Orion announced the failed endpoints by press release in 2020.
graveyard.note_extra: A peripheral target - the diaphragm - and directly relevant to Alex, whose supine FVC is 61%.

graveyard.name: biib078
graveyard.note: antisense knockdown of C9orf72 repeat RNA; no clinical benefit
graveyard.note_extra: The anchor case for arrived_failed. Delivered intrathecally, so it bypassed the barrier entirely, and postmortem analysis of halted C9orf72 ASO trial tissue found drug present in brain and spinal cord without stopping the disease drivers. Delivery was not the problem here; the biology was.

graveyard.name: sodium phenylbutyrate-taurursodiol
graveyard.note: eased ER stress and mitochondrial dysfunction; no ALSFRS-R benefit at 48 weeks
graveyard.note_extra: AMX0035, marketed as Relyvrio in the US and Albrioza in Canada. Approved in Canada in 2022 under Notice of Compliance with Conditions on the 137-patient phase 2 CENTAUR trial, explicitly conditional on a confirmatory phase 3. PHOENIX (n=664) missed its primary endpoint on 2024-03-08 (p=0.667) and every secondary; Amylyx began withdrawing both authorizations on 2024-04-04, with the Canadian market withdrawal deadline set at 2024-12-31. A two-component mixture, so expect component B to handle it poorly - the SMILES is a salt plus a conjugate.

graveyard.name: tauroursodeoxycholic acid
graveyard.note: bile acid blunting ER stress and apoptosis; missed ALSFRS-R and survival endpoints
graveyard.note_extra: The taurursodiol half of AMX0035, tested alone, and it failed too. Useful for the pitch: the combination and its component both failed independently.

graveyard.name: arimoclomol
graveyard.note: amplified heat-shock protein response; no gain on function-survival composite
graveyard.verify_note: Orphazyme announced the failure publicly in 2021; the Lancet Neurology paper cited here is 2024.

graveyard.name: verdiperstat
graveyard.trial_name: HEALEY ALS Platform Trial regimen B (NCT04297683)
graveyard.note: myeloperoxidase inhibitor against neuroinflammation; no slowing of disease progression
graveyard.verify_note: All four HEALEY regimens stopped dosing in 2022; the JAMA-family papers are 2025.

graveyard.name: zilucoplan
graveyard.trial_name: HEALEY ALS Platform Trial regimen A (NCT04297683)
graveyard.note: complement C5 inhibitor; stopped early for futility, progression unchanged
graveyard.note_extra: A macrocyclic peptide with a PEG chain and a palmitoyl tail, around 3.5 kDa. It has a SMILES but it is far outside any BBB training set, so component B should report it out of domain.

graveyard.name: pridopidine
graveyard.trial_name: HEALEY ALS Platform Trial regimen D (NCT04297683)
graveyard.note: sigma-1 receptor agonist for neuroprotection; disease rate ratio 0.99, no benefit
graveyard.note_extra: A rate ratio of 0.99 is as close to no effect as a trial can report.

graveyard.name: cnm-au8
graveyard.trial_name: HEALEY ALS Platform Trial regimen C (NCT04297683)
graveyard.note: gold nanocrystal boosting neuronal NAD+ energetics; no ALSFRS-R or survival benefit
graveyard.note_extra: A suspension of gold nanocrystals. There is no molecule here at all, which makes it the cleanest demonstration of why an applicability-domain guard has to exist.

graveyard.name: erythropoietin
graveyard.note: recombinant EPO for neuroprotection; did not change the course of ALS
graveyard.verify_note: Glycoprotein, ~30 kDa. PubChem CID 92043599 'Epoetin Alfa' is a C42H73NO16 glycan fragment, not the protein, so citing it would be misleading - identifier left as the trial registration.

graveyard.name: pioglitazone
graveyard.note: PPAR-gamma agonist added to riluzole; stopped for futility, no survival gain
graveyard.note_extra: Tested as an add-on to riluzole, so it is also the closest analogue in the graveyard to what we are actually screening for: something to give Alex alongside the riluzole he already takes.

graveyard.name: glatiramer acetate
graveyard.note: immunomodulatory copolymer; primary and secondary endpoints both missed
graveyard.verify_note: A random copolymer of four amino acids with no single defined structure, so no SMILES exists even in principle. Teva's release is 2008; the journal paper is 2009 (PMID 19922128).
